Today, Freya Axelsen had every chance of setting a new record. Right now, three hundred and fifty thousand people were watching her stream, and that number was climbing fast as the broadcast moved into the Q&A segment.

If the live viewer count hit four hundred thousand, it would be an all-time world record for the entire coaching industry.

No one before her had ever pulled it off. Even the famous and obscenely wealthy Tony Bobbins had only drawn three hundred and ninety thousand in his prime—and that was after decades in the business and with a face the whole world recognized! Now Freya had a shot at shattering that ceiling with room to spare, securing her fame for years to come. And if anyone thought it was just dumb luck, Freya knew better: fortune favors only prepared minds and hands ready to act.

At first, things had gone only reasonably well. An hour went to a lecture on how to achieve your goals. That was the most enjoyable part, though only a hundred thousand viewers showed up. Expected, yet well below par for Freya, with her four million followers on Instagram and another twelve million on TikTok. Freya wasn't fond of the latter because it lacked a serious audience, but the algorithms had other plans.

Another hour was taken up by questions along the lines of "the best age to launch a startup" and "how to get off the couch and get things done," which followers had submitted via a form before the stream. The questions landed well and pushed the live count up to two hundred thousand.

Even so, it wasn't enough. It was a plateau. Two hundred thousand—a plateau that grew harder to break through every single time.

And that was when Freya made her power move, as the New York hustlers liked to put it. Within twenty minutes, right in the middle of the stream, her assistants rigged up a payment form and blasted posts across social media. That kicked off the surprise portion of the broadcast: open questions for donations. Unmoderated, but on Freya's terms.
